There are two models I'm aware of that might fit what you're talking about. Neither of which is a realistic possible given current state of the art, but might be given substantial improvement in engineering ability down the line.

The first is a Bussard Ramjet, which collects interstellar hydrogen and uses it to fuel a fusion rocket. Beyond the whole 'we haven't even figured out fusion' thing, the energy to fuse hydrogen is pretty intense, there's no guarantee it's energy positive sans a gravity well to bring it all together, unless we push it to post helium reactions (which is ever farther beyond state of the art).

The other is a model of using magnetic fields to grab hold of interstellar iron (very rare but it exists) and accelerate it backwards at relativistic speeds to make up for the tiny amount of mass.

Both of these still have speed limits though, the energy of impacting interstellar hydrogen increases exponentially with velocity, and the number of impacts goes up too (once relativity starts coming into play it gets even crazier since they have more mass as well as more speed). Also you have to factor in issues with the amount of stuff around being a variable, which helps reduce the issue of cooking re-entry style from your velocity, but also takes away possible reaction mass.

This could be a very messy time for Android over next few months. Here is the real issue and why Apple is better equipped to handle something like this. Android, in its fervor to allow customization, could put out a fix tomorrow for this, but because all the vendors AND telcos put their own builds of the software on your phones it could take up to a year to get a damn update, IF they update at all. Now I expect the Nexus line to be corrected instantly, but this showcases a if not THE largest issue currently with android.

The fix, IMO, for Google would be to ban/disallow companies to make their own builds and instead give them the access/tools to build ON TOP of the base load with downloadable apps. So for verizon/samsung the phone could come preloaded with touchwiz interface, but as a separate app and the user can chose to scrap it. This was, android can be updated all the time on time and if any one app breaks from an update then the onus is 100% on the vendor who puts that app out and the customer can chose security/updates over the apps possibly breaking. While this is not a perfect solution as who wants broken apps, it allows the customers to make the choices, or hell go base system with no damn bloat shit all over it. Additionally the benefit is people like Samsung can allow others to use their interfaces and possibly get new customers to come over to their phones if they like what they see.
